case_evidence.description: Frozen Python 1.2 public src/eyetrajectoriespy/plotting.py::plot_sparse_fpca_covariance. Real fitted univariate sparse PACE latent covariance heatmap, preserving scientific evaluation times, fitted covariance matrix, Matplotlib image lower origin, source title and source axes/viridis color limits.

Accepted domain: genuine native R fitted sparse covariance/PACE scientific result class etr_sparse_fpca_native, finite increasing evaluation grid, finite n-by-n covariance and matching eigensystem. Default R plot remains unchanged. Strict source scientific geometry does not accept external Python ax injection; it will not impersonate Python Matplotlib objects.

Native source image stores the actual fitted Gaussian PACE latent covariance matrix, data grid extent (g0,gmax,g0,gmax), min/max scientific image normalization, source plot titles and labels. Committed pinned Python 1.2 tests create public SparseFPCAResult using the exact native population arrays and directly compare public plot get_array, get_extent, get_clim and source colormap name. A fitted native 24-curve sparse population fixture is used; exact-head CI not witnessed green.

Strict source refuses non-native fitted result, missing/malformed covariance and any nonfinite entry, unknown source fields and nonlogical strict flag. Native R error classes and Matplotlib ax injection are distinct and no claim of Python runtime class/exception parity is made.

Frozen Python returns a Matplotlib Axes with one imshow image plus an attached figure colorbar. Native R draws on base R and returns a typed one-panel source-scientific artist record including exactly the original fitted covariance array, source image extent, vmin/vmax, declared viridis cmap, plot axis labels, title and colorbar label. Not a live Matplotlib Axes or identical pixels.

Visual display of the genuine fitted univariate sparse FPCA/PACE latent covariance operator, retaining any PSD projection and original evaluation grid rather than an alternative fdapace fit or raw-data interpolation.
